Smt. Rinki And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. Through Principal ... on 2 September, 2025

G.A. 
 Court No. - 70
 Hon'Ble Dr. Gautam Chowdhary, J. 
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2.  The present application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Complaint Case No. 19807 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Eka, District Firozabad, with the prayer that in the event of arrest, applicants may be released on anticipatory bail.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant Nos. 1 to 3 are the in-laws of the deceased whereas applicant No. 4 is her husband.

Earlier an F.I.R. was lodged by the informant in the year 2019 with regard to the incident took place on 16.10.2019, in which the married daughter of informant died due to burning for non fulfillment of demand of additional dowry.

During investigation the dying declaration of informant's daughter was also recorded in which she stated that her brother-in-law namely Praveen makes quarrel on account of which she committed suicide by burning herself and no one is involved in the alleged incident.

After investigation was completed the charge sheet under Section 306 IPC was filed against the said co-accused, Praveen Kumar and the names of other accused, i.e., present applicants were exonerated meaning thereby final report was submitted in their favour.

Learned counsel further submits that it is settled law that if some accused have been charge sheeted and some accused have been exonerated in the charge sheet the informant has an alternative remedy to challenge the same by filing protest petition and/ or to move an appropriate application under Section 319 Cr.P.C. at the trial of charge sheeted accused for summoning of other accused who have been exonerated in the charge sheet, but instead of doing so the informant has registered a fresh complaint case for the same incident.

Learned counsel further submits that after the complaint case was registered the statements under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. were recorded and the applicants have been summoned, which is against the settled principle of law.
He further submits that since summoning order has been passed against the applicants, therefore, applicants have an apprehension that they may be arrested in the above mentioned case.
It has further been submitted that applicants have no criminal antecedent.
The applicants undertake to cooperate during trial and they would appear as and when required by the Court.
It has been stated that in case, applicants are granted anticipatory bail, they shall not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate with the trial and would obey all conditions of bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. for the State has opposed the application for anticipatory bail, but could not dispute the facts asserted on behalf of applicants.

5. It may be stated that in case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court Smt. Rinki And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. Through Principal ... on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159573170/
2 must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.
6.

sentences.text:
In the instant case, considering the settled principle of law regarding anticipatory bail,
submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on merit of the case, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.
7. The anticipatory bail application is allowed.

8. In the event of arrest of the applicants-Smt. Rinki, Satish, Smt. Nema Devi and Hem Singh,
involved in the aforesaid case crime shall be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial on their furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- each with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(i) Applicants shall attend the court proceedings as and when required and shall not sought any unnecessary adjournment.

(ii) Applicants shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise or to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) Applicants shall cooperate during trial and would not misuse the liberty of bail.
9. In default of any of the conditions, the court concerned shall be at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicants.

(Dr. Gautam Chowdhary,J.) September 2, 2025 Mustaqeem.
